successCriteria.description: All nine concrete files exist and compile: PgEmployeeRepository + EmployeeService, PgLeaveTypeRepository, PgLeavePolicyRepository + PolicyService, PgLeaveBalanceRepository + BalanceService, PgAuditLogRepository + AuditService — each implementing the interface declared in its module's *.model.ts.

BalanceService implements the binding counter semantics exactly: availableDays = entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays (derived, never stored); SUBMIT n → pendingDays += n; APPROVE → pendingDays -= n, usedDays += n; REJECT pending → pendingDays -= n; CANCEL pending → pendingDays -= n; CANCEL approved → usedDays -= n.

A balance transition that would take any counter (usedDays or pendingDays) below zero throws an error (never clamps), and the negative guard exists only in BalanceService — no other module duplicates it.

Every repository and service method accepts an optional PoolClient as its LAST parameter and passes it through to the underlying data access; when omitted, the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts is used.

BalanceService methods accept the day count n as a parameter (reserve/approve/reject/cancel take `days`), and do not compute the day count themselves — the caller computes n via the shared countLeaveDays helper (Phase 4).

Each repository persists and returns the entity it was asked to create/update (create returns the persisted row; update returns the updated row), and lookup methods return the entity or null/[] per the interface contract.
AuditService.record persists an AuditLog row (via the repository) and returns it; the AuditLog is immutable once written (no update/delete operations exist).
The build gate passes: `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) succeeds with strict TypeScript and no `any` (use `unknown` + type guards), and no database access occurs outside the repository layer.

constraints: No tests in this phase — unit tests for these modules are Phase 4 (part 3/3).
No controllers/routes/HTTP surface in this phase — only repository + service implementations.
All database access goes through the repository layer (GP-001); services never issue SQL/ORM calls directly.
No cross-module imports in this phase: the five leaf modules depend only on src/shared/types/ and the pg PoolClient type (per the reconciled dependency map).
remainingDays is never independently persisted — it is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays.
Negative guards live ONLY in BalanceService and are never duplicated into callers or other modules.
Use `unknown` with type guards instead of `any` (HARNESS constraint no-any); no hardcoded secrets; no @gestalt/* packages as dependencies.
outOfScope: Unit tests for these repositories/services (Phase 4, part 3/3).
The leave module orchestrator, countLeaveDays helper, controllers, and routes (Phase 4).
RBAC enforcement and auth guards — no HTTP/API boundary exists in this phase.
Accrual, carry-over, and fiscal-year boundary logic (binding rule 2: none exist).

ambiguities.description: Whether the concrete repositories use Knex (per HARNESS "Knex migrations + thin repository layer") or raw pg queries. The interfaces only expose PoolClient, so the implementation shape is open.
options: Either, as long as it goes through the repository layer

ambiguities.description: Whether the balance service's negative guard should also enforce the sufficiency check (n <= availableDays) at reserve time, or leave sufficiency to the Phase 4 leave orchestrator. The binding rule places the sufficiency check at approval; reserve-time enforcement is unspecified.
options: Enforce n <= availableDays at reserve too
Only enforce non-negative counters; leave sufficiency to approval (Phase 4)
Enforce at reserve as a safety net but keep approval as the authoritative check

ambiguities.description: Whether the balance service should recompute/update the derived remainingDays field on the returned entity after a counter change, given the model still carries a remainingDays field (documented as derived, never independently persisted).
options: Return the entity with remainingDays recomputed in-memory
Return the entity with remainingDays as stored (stale) and rely on getAvailableDays

entityInvariants.invariant: usedDays and pendingDays are always non-negative integers; availableDays is always derived as totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays and never stored; a write that would make either counter negative is rejected with an error, never clamped.
Immutable once created — only create/read operations exist; no update or delete path.
employmentStatus is one of ACTIVE | INACTIVE | TERMINATED; terminate() transitions the employee to TERMINATED and records a terminationDate.
isActive governs eligibility; deactivate() transitions a policy to inactive without deleting it.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws an error (never clamps) if pendingDays + days would exceed availableDays or go negative; returns the updated LeaveBalance.
Moves days from pendingDays to usedDays (pendingDays -= n, usedDays += n); throws if pendingDays would go below zero; returns the updated LeaveBalance.
Releases pending days (pendingDays -= n); throws if pendingDays would go below zero; returns the updated LeaveBalance.
For PENDING releases pendingDays -= n; for APPROVED restores usedDays -= n; throws if the relevant counter would go below zero; returns the updated LeaveBalance.
Pure derivation returning totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays; never reads or writes a stored remainingDays.
Persists and returns an AuditLog; performedAt is set at write time; performedBy may be null.
Transitions the employee to TERMINATED with a terminationDate; throws NotFoundError if the employee does not exist.
Sets isActive=false and returns the updated policy; throws NotFoundError if the policy does not exist.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Concrete classes must implement the exact interface signatures (method names, parameter order, optional PoolClient as last param, return types) declared in each module's *.model.ts.
When the optional client is omitted, use the shared `pool` exported from connection.ts; never create a new Pool.
Reuse the shared error types (NotFoundError, ValidationError, InsufficientBalanceError, etc.) for all thrown errors; do not introduce ad-hoc error shapes.
LeaveType.code must use the shared LeaveTypeCode type imported from src/shared/types/ (not a redeclared literal).
Balance counter semantics must match the binding rule: availableDays = entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays, with only the five permitted writes and no negative counters.

integrationPoints.why: All repositories default to this pool when no unit-of-work client is passed.
Leaf modules import shared types and error classes; the only permitted dependency.
Optional last parameter threaded through repository and service methods so Phase 4's leave orchestrator can run status change + balance + audit in one transaction.
